name: create_location
description: Add a new location to the campaign. Use it when the story reaches a place that does not exist yet. Names must be unique among locations and NPCs, and a name that repeats an existing place in other words (such as 'Market Street' for 'Market Road') is refused. Set discovered to true only when anyone in the world would have heard of the place, so the player already knows it. A place given a map point (x and y) must lie inside a region of the map with at least 0.5 km of ground between the point and the region's edge; if none does, the refusal says so, and you must create that region with create_region first. To put a place inside another, give parent set to the name of that top-level location; such a place has no map point of its own, so leave out x and y.

description.description: What the place looks, sounds, and smells like, in a sentence or two.

discovered.description: True if the player already knows the place, because it is famous or the story has revealed it. False by default.

x.description: Kilometers east of the map's center; negative for west. Give x and y together, or neither to leave the place off the map. Only when the place's position relative to others is known; do not use 0 as a default.

y.description: Kilometers north of the map's center; negative for south. Give x and y together, or neither. Only when the place's position relative to others is known.

force.description: Set true only to put this place on a point another place already has, as when two places are the same spot. Without it, a point another place already has is refused.

parent.description: The name of the top-level location this place is inside. Leave it out for a place on the map. A place with a parent cannot be given x or y.

name: create_region
description: Add an area of ground to the world map, drawn as a coloured shape. It stays hidden from the player until it is discovered or a discovered place lies inside it; set discovered to true only when the player would know of this ground already. Use it when the story establishes a lake, a crater field, or other terrain that the map does not show yet, and when a new place with a map point needs ground around it. The terrain names a kind of ground the rule set defines; if the name is not a kind, the refusal lists the kinds. Give points as the corners of the shape in order around its edge, each as [x, y] in kilometers from the map's center, with x positive east and y positive north. Use only corners the story has given you, drawing the outline as closely as the story supports. A name must be unique among regions. A region that overlaps another is refused; set force to true only when the two really do overlap, as when one is the other's marsh.

name.description: The region's name, such as 'West Lake'.

terrain.description: The id of the terrain kind this ground is.

points.description: The corners of the region's outline, in order around its edge. At least three.

discovered.description: Set true only when the player already knows of this ground. Without it, the region stays hidden until a discovered place lies inside it.

force.description: Set true only to let this region overlap another region on purpose. Without it, an overlap is refused.

name: create_npc
description: Add an NPC to the campaign and place them at an existing location. Leave personality, accent, or quirks out to have them generated at random; give them only when the story calls for a specific trait. Give character options, such as appearance or biography, only when the story calls for them; anything left out is rolled or left blank. A name that matches a published statblock, such as a creature in the source material, takes that statblock's stats, armor, and attacks, so leave the stats out of the character options. Names must be unique among locations and NPCs.

location.description: The name of the location the NPC is at. It must already exist.

description.description: Who the NPC is: appearance, role, and what they are doing.

pronouns.description: Optional. The NPC's pronouns, such as "she/her", "he/him", or "they/them", or another form. Record them whenever the NPC is written in the text, so the GM does not have to guess.

personality.description: Optional. How the NPC carries themselves.

accent.description: Optional. How the NPC sounds when they speak.

quirks.description: Optional. Habits or mannerisms the NPC shows.

force.description: Set true only to create a custom NPC under the name of a published statblock. Without it, such a name is refused if stats are given.

name: move_actor
description: Move the player character or an NPC to another existing location. Use it when someone travels or is sent somewhere. Travel follows the routes in the location descriptions: send the player character only to a place reached by a route from where they are, and never to a place they have not heard of, unless something forces them there (a trap, a teleporter, or some other force). A forced move discovers the place on arrival. The player character starts unplaced, so on the first turn create the place where the story begins and move the player character there. Moving the player character to a place discovers it. Leave location out to send an NPC into the wind: it is at no location until a later move brings it back. The player character cannot go into the wind. Always give the mode. Use overland for a journey across open country or between distant sites, which takes travel time and needs a route. Use in_settlement for a walk within one settlement, station, or site, which takes time at the travel speed. Use in_dungeon for a move through a building, ship, or ruin, which takes no clock time. The result reports the time charged.

name.description: The name of the player character or of the NPC who moves.

location.description: The name of the location to move them to. It must already exist. Omit it only to send an NPC into the wind.

mode.description: How the move is made: overland (a journey across open country, needs a route), in_settlement (a walk within a settlement, takes time at the travel speed), or in_dungeon (no clock time). NPC moves take no clock time whatever the mode.

route.description: Required for an overland move, and ignored for other modes. Describe the journey. path: the kind of path the party follows (the names the rule set gives). distance: short, medium, or long. terrain: the hardest ground on the route. vast: 0 to 2, how wide and empty the land is. weather_choice: when conditions on the day make travel harder, the choice the rule set gives for it. The names of path, distance, and terrain come from the rule set.

name: add_note
description: Record a note for yourself as the GM, to track events, updates, and situations so you stay consistent. It is not written for the player. Attach it to a location or NPC by giving its name as the subject; leave the subject out for a note about the campaign as a whole. The result includes the note's id, for later update_note or delete_note calls.

text.description: The fact to remember, written as a complete sentence.

subject.description: Optional. The name of the location or NPC the note is about.

name: search_notes
description: Search your GM notes on events, updates, and situations, to stay consistent. Every word in the query must appear in the note's text or in its subject's name. Each result includes the note's id. Use it before continuing a thread or answering questions about what has happened before.

name: append_journal
description: Add text to the end of the journal the player reads, a text file of what has happened in the campaign in the story's own voice. Start a new campaign day's passage with it; to add to a day that already has one, merge the text into that passage with replace_in_journal instead. Do not reveal what the player character has not learned.

text.description: The text to add, one or more sentences in the past tense. Begin it with the campaign day, as in 'Day 3: ...'.

name: replace_in_journal
description: Edit the journal by replacing one passage with another, like an exact find and replace. old_text must be copied exactly from the journal and match in one place only. An empty new_text deletes the passage. Use it to correct facts and to condense the journal when it runs long.

old_text.description: The exact passage to replace, copied from the journal. Quote enough of it to match only once.

new_text.description: The text that replaces it. Empty to delete the passage.

name: search_journal
description: Search the journal the player reads, to stay consistent with what the player has been told. Matching is fuzzy, so near spellings count. Each result gives the line numbers it covers, for view_journal.

context.description: Lines to include before and after each match, from 0 to 3. Defaults to 1.

name: view_journal
description: View lines of the journal the player reads, numbered from 1, by line range. Shows at most 50 lines at a time. Use it to read a stretch in full, such as the lines around a search result.

start_line.description: The first line to view, from 1.

end_line.description: The last line to view. Defaults to start_line.

name: all_at_location
description: Look up a location: its description, the NPCs there (with personality, accent, and quirks), whether the player character is there, and the notes about the place or those NPCs. Leave out the location to look at the player character's current location. Use it whenever you need to know what is in a place before you narrate it or act in it.

location.description: The location's name. Leave it out for the player character's location.

name: search_location
description: Find locations by words in their name or description. Every word in the query must appear. Use it to find a place you have described before or to check whether a place already exists before you create one.

name: search_npc
description: Find NPCs anywhere in the world by words in their name, location, description, personality, accent, or quirks. Every word in the query must appear. Each result gives the NPC's location. Use it to check whether an NPC already exists before you create one, or to find someone the story mentions.

name: get_statblock
description: Get a character's statblock: stats, template, features, and fields. Works for the player character and for NPCs. Statblocks are not in your context until you fetch them, so fetch one before a roll, before a change to a character's abilities or gear, or whenever their capabilities matter to the outcome.

name: character_options
description: List the values a character field can take, for create_npc's character option. Call it with no field to list the fields that take a value from a table. Call it with a field to list that field's values, with a description of what each named option does.

field.description: The field to list, from the fields that take a table value.

name: lookup_rule
description: Read the full text of a rule. Your context lists every rule with a brief and shows the important rules in full. Read a rule you only have the brief of before you rely on it.

rule.description: The rule's id, as listed in your context.

name: list_lookups
description: List everything you can look up, each with a short brief: the lookup tools, the rules, and the locations and NPCs in the world. Use it when you are unsure what exists. Then look up the full entry with the matching tool.

name: speak
description: Get the exact words an NPC says. A separate step writes the dialogue from the NPC's personality, accent, and quirks, so give the intent, not the words. The NPC should be at the player character's location; if not, nothing is written and a warning is returned, unless force is true. In combat, speak only for a line that changes what the player must decide. Quote the returned dialogue as it is.

intent.description: What the NPC wants to say or achieve in this moment.

replace.description: Set true to rewrite the line already queued for this NPC in this reply, for example to amend it before the next line. Without it, a second call for the same NPC is refused.

force.description: Set true to speak an NPC who is not at the player character's location, for example across a wall or by message. The narration will say they are speaking from elsewhere. Without it, an absent NPC gets a warning and no dialogue.

name: update_location
description: Change a location's description. Move it on the map by giving x and y, or take it off the map by setting off_map to true. A place inside another cannot be given x or y. Its name stays the same. Leave x, y, and off_map out to keep its position. It never moves a character: to take the player character or an NPC into a place, use move_actor. Use delete_location instead to remove the place from the story.

description.description: The new description of the place, in a sentence or two.

x.description: Kilometers east of the map's center; negative for west. Give x and y together, or neither to leave the place off the map. Only when the place's position relative to others is known; do not use 0 as a default.

y.description: Kilometers north of the map's center; negative for south. Give x and y together. Only when the place's position relative to others is known.

off_map.description: True to take the place off the map, for example when its position is no longer known. It stays in the story and keeps its description. Do not give x or y with it. False by default.

force.description: Set true only to put this place on a point another place already has, as when two places are the same spot. Without it, a point another place already has is refused.

name: discover_location
description: Mark an existing location as discovered: the player character has heard about it in detail, or the story has revealed it. A discovered location appears on the player's map. Moving the player character there discovers it too, so use this for places they learn of without going. When an NPC gives directions, discover only the destination; do not discover the other places the directions name. The player sees only the summary, never the location's full description, so pass a summary with no GM-only detail. Keep the summary brief: one short sentence, a rumor or first impression, not a paraphrase of the full description. Giving a summary for a location that is already discovered replaces what the player sees of it.

summary.description: Optional. One short sentence the player sees of the location, ideally under 120 characters and never more than 300. Do not copy the full description. Write what the player character has heard or can see, not secrets, hidden contents, or the full description. Without it, the player sees only the name.

name: delete_location
description: Remove a location from the campaign. It is refused while any character is still there; move them first, and refused while places are inside it; remove those first. Notes about the location are kept.

name: hire_hireling
description: Hire a character into a player character's company. The hireling has a rolled sheet like an NPC's and is controlled by the player. Its wage is paid in the rule set's currency from the employer each new day, and an employer who cannot pay is reported as unpaid. The employer must be a player character who has a location. Give the wage the hireling asks for, or the marketplace's listed wage for a hireling listed there. Leave personality, accent, or quirks out to have them rolled. Names must be unique among locations and characters.

employer.description: The name of the player character who hires them. The wage comes from this character's money.

wage.description: Money per day, in the rule set's currency, zero or more.

description.description: Who the hireling is: appearance, role, and what they are good for.

personality.description: Optional. How the hireling carries themselves.

accent.description: Optional. How the hireling sounds when they speak.

quirks.description: Optional. Habits or mannerisms the hireling shows.

pronouns.description: Optional. The hireling's pronouns, such as "she/her", "he/him", or "they/them", or another form. Record them whenever the hireling is written in the text, so the GM does not have to guess.

name: dismiss_hireling
description: Remove a hireling from its employer's company. It stays where it is and becomes an ordinary NPC. Use this when the story has the hireling leave, for example when its wage went unpaid and it goes, or when it chooses to go. Give the cause in a few words.

cause.description: Why the hireling leaves, in a few words.

name: change_currency
description: Give a character money from outside a purchase (a gift, a reward, a loan repaid, a loot split), or take it away (a fine, a toll, a bribe, a debt paid to someone else). Use a positive amount to give and a negative amount to take. A take is refused if the character lacks the money; there is no credit. Give the cause in a few words. Do not use this for anything bought in a shop, and do not use it to make up money the story has not earned.

amount.description: Money to give (positive) or take (negative), in the rule set's currency.

cause.description: Why the money changes hands, in a few words.

name: place_object
description: Put a world object in a place: a location or an area inside one. It holds what the story has stocked there, such as money, an item, or a described thing. Give a short name a character can take it by, such as 'sealed crate', and a fuller description in contents. Optionally give money or an item name. Set hidden when the object is not yet found; a hidden object cannot be seen or taken. Use this only for treasure or objects the story has placed; do not invent them unprompted. Do not place an object again when the place already holds it: check the objects listed for the place in the scene first, and when the object is already there, leave it be.

place.description: The location, or the area inside it, that holds the object.

name.description: A short name to take the object by, such as 'sealed crate' or 'chest'. Keep it to one to three words.

contents.description: A description of the object, such as 'a dented canister with some currency inside'.

hidden.description: True if the object is not yet found.

reason.description: Why the object is placed, in a few words.

currency.description: Money in the object, in the rule set's currency, if any.

item.description: The name of an item in the object, if any.

item_size.description: The size of the item, if one is given. Defaults to normal.

name: take_object
description: A character takes a visible object from the place they are in. Money goes to that character. An item goes into their inventory, and the take is refused if it does not fit. Use this only when a character acts to take the object.

object.description: The object's description, as the GM gave it.

reason.description: Why the character takes it, in a few words.

name: update_npc
description: Change an NPC's details. Only the fields you give change; the rest stay as they are. Giving quirks replaces the whole list. Use it when an NPC changes, for example after a shift in attitude or appearance. The player character cannot be changed this way. A story-only NPC has no stats until you give them with character, armor, and attacks; this works once, and it refuses an NPC that already has stats.

description.description: Optional. Who the NPC is now: appearance, role, and what they are doing.

personality.description: Optional. How the NPC carries themselves now.

accent.description: Optional. How the NPC sounds when they speak.

quirks.description: Optional. The NPC's full list of habits or mannerisms, replacing the old list.

armor.description: Optional, for a story-only NPC being given stats. What each hit against them absorbs.

attacks.description: Optional, for a story-only NPC being given stats. The NPC's attacks, each with a name and dice such as '1d8' or '1d6+1d6'.

dice.description: The damage dice, such as '1d8' or '1d6+1d6'.

flags.description: Leave out for a plain attack. The flags the rule set defines for attacks.

name: delete_npc
description: Remove an NPC from the campaign. Use it for a temporary NPC who matters little to the story, such as a passing stranger, a hired guard, or a monster from a fight, once they have left the scene or the encounter they were in has ended. Keep NPCs the story may bring back, and remove an NPC who leaves the story or dies only when they are no longer needed. Notes about them are kept. The player character cannot be removed.

name: update_note
description: Change the text of one of your GM notes, identified by its id. Use it when something you recorded has changed.

note_id.description: The id of the note, as given by add_note or search_notes.

text.description: The corrected fact, written as a complete sentence.

name: delete_note
description: Remove one of your GM notes, identified by its id, once it no longer holds true or matters.

note_id.description: The id of the note, as given by add_note or search_notes.

name: ooc
description: Mark the player's message as out of character: they talk to you as the GM rather than to their character, ask about the rules or the world, or ask for a change outside the story. Call it in place of the other tools for the message. An out-of-character step then replies to the player directly and has all the tools. Set no_narration when the reply needs no story beat after it.

no_narration.description: Set true when the out-of-character reply is the whole response. Leave it false, the default, when the story should move on after the reply, which is then narrated.

name: create_encounter_map
description: Create an encounter map: a grid of cells set in an existing location, where a tactical encounter takes place. Use it before starting an encounter there. Cells are scaled by the rule set's grid.

name.description: A name for the map, unique among maps.

location.description: The name of the existing location the map is set in.

columns.description: How many cells wide the map is, from 1 to 60. Required unless a template is given; with a template, it overrides the template's width.

rows.description: How many cells tall the map is, from 1 to 60. Required unless a template is given; with a template, it overrides the template's height.

description.description: What the map shows: terrain, cover, hazards, and anything else that matters for tactics.

template.description: A standard layout, such as room or corridor. The template sets the size and the starting terrain. Leave it out for an empty map.

name: update_encounter_map
description: Change an encounter map: its name, the location it is in, its size, or its description. Refused if the new name is taken or a participant would be left outside the new size.

name.description: The name of the map to change.

columns.description: How many cells wide the map is, from 1 to 60.

rows.description: How many cells tall the map is, from 1 to 60.

new_name.description: A new name for the map. Leave out to keep the current name.

location.description: The name of the location the map is in. Leave out to keep the current location.

name: delete_encounter_map
description: Delete an encounter map. Refused while an encounter is using it.

name.description: The name of the map to delete.

name: start_encounter
description: Start an encounter on an encounter map. Its location becomes the encounter's location. Only one encounter can be in progress at a time. Add participants after starting. The player character and NPCs take turns in the order they join.

map.description: The name of the encounter map to play on.

name: end_encounter
description: End the encounter in progress. Any turn in progress ends with it.

name: add_participant
description: Add a character to the encounter in progress, on a side. Player characters default to the party and NPCs to the foes. The turn order keeps each side together: the party first, then the other sides in the order they first appear. A character who is not at the encounter's location is still added, and the result carries a warning to act on.

name.description: The name of the player character or of an NPC.

side.description: The side the character fights on, such as party or foes. Any name works. Leave it out for the default.

name: remove_participant
description: Take a character out of the encounter in progress. If they are taking their turn, it ends and the next participant's turn follows.

name.description: The name of the participant to remove.

name: place_participant
description: Put a participant on a cell of the encounter map, counted from 0 at the top left: column increases to the right and row increases downward. Moving is limited to the rule set's movement per turn, counted in cells moved in a straight line or diagonal. Obstacles block: a cell with a blocking object cannot be entered or be the destination, so the participant goes around it. Terrain that costs extra movement to enter takes that many moves for each cell entered. That limit applies only to the participant whose turn it is; moving anyone else is free, though they still cannot enter a blocked cell. The first placement is free. Use this to move a participant, not to tell the story of how they got there.

name.description: The name of the participant to place.

column.description: The cell's column, from 0 at the left edge.

row.description: The cell's row, from 0 at the top edge.

name: set_map_cells
description: Set the terrain or object on cells of an encounter map. A cell with an object that blocks cannot be entered.

map.description: The name of the encounter map.

cells.description: The cells to change, at most 200 per call. Each cell needs a column and row, and terrain or object or both. Give an empty string for terrain or object to clear it.

column.description: The cell's column, from 0 at the left edge.

row.description: The cell's row, from 0 at the top edge.

terrain.description: The terrain id for the cell, such as mud or floor. Empty clears it.

object.description: The object id on the cell, such as wall or crate. Empty clears it.

name: end_turn
description: End the turn of the NPC whose turn it is in the encounter. Call it once the NPC's action is resolved. Player characters end their own turns, so do not use this for them.

name.description: The name of the NPC whose turn is ending.
